page: OVHcloud b3-128 is a General Purpose cloud instance provisioned via KVM virtualization. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs built on AMD EPYC x86_64 processors running at a base clock of 2.3 GHz, with hyper-threading disabled (1 thread per core). Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes a bundled 400 GB local NVMe SSD, baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark performance exhibits top-tier multi-threaded processing and memory throughput. The server registered a multi-core stress-ng metric of 98,377.64 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,588.0, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Large-block read memory bandwidth reached 281.24 GB/sec alongside 145.9 GB/sec write bandwidth, contributing to strong results in memory-bound operations such as Redis SET (74.67 million operations/sec) and PassMark database operations (30,713.31). Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,874.0 and gzip compression speed of 28.81 GB/sec, placed in the middle 50%.

Given its dedicated core allocation and balanced resource distribution, the b3-128 offers consistent compute output without multi-tenant thread contention. The instance achieves a solid qualitative balance between memory volume, multi-core parallelism, and high-speed local NVMe storage. Tradeoffs include the lack of AVX-512 extensions and average single-thread execution speeds, making it better fitted for horizontally scaled, concurrent tasks than latency-sensitive single-threaded pipelines.

OVHcloud b3-128 is appropriate for high-concurrency production deployments. Key target workloads include distributed in-memory databases, Clang-based software compilation pipelines, continuous integration systems, container orchestration nodes, and medium-scale backend database processing.
